name: clip-trimmer

frames.best_why: The trimmed range, ruler and playhead are all visible while it plays, with the kept length shown below.

tagline: Drag orange handles along a filmstrip to choose the seconds you keep.
summary: A video trimming card with a preview image, a ten-frame filmstrip and a ruler. Two orange handles set the start and end of the kept clip, dimming what gets cut, and a playhead loops over the selection.
appearance: A dark rounded card holding a wide mountain preview in a rounded frame, with a timestamp pill and a round play button on it. Beneath sits a thin filmstrip crossed by two orange handles, a small ruler labelled in seconds, and a kept-length line.
behaviour: Dragging a handle narrows or widens the kept range, snapping to whole seconds and dimming the trimmed footage; dragging between the handles slides the whole clip. The playhead loops inside the selection, and Reset restores the full length.
demo_content: A panoramic photo of snowy mountain peaks above a sea of clouds, 12 seconds long.
search_phrases: drag handles to cut a clip
filmstrip with start and end markers
choose a section of a video
use_when: A clip, recording or media file needs a quick in and out point before upload or export.
avoid_when: It trims numbers only, not real footage, so you must swap in your own preview and frame images.
customise: Props set the preview image and alt text, clip duration, starting range, minimum length and a range-change callback; the filmstrip frame count and colours stay fixed.
weight_why: One image and ten thumbnails; a frame loop runs only while playback is on.

a11y.note: Handles are labelled sliders with keyboard steps, but playback and transitions ignore reduced-motion.

issues: The filmstrip and preview use one still panorama, so every frame looks alike.
polish_why: Convincing, tactile trimmer with snapping and a tidy ruler; the preview is a static stand-in.
